title: Free-radical chlorination of methane
caption: UV light splits Cl₂ into two chlorine radicals (initiation). Each Cl• takes an H from methane, and the methyl radical takes a Cl from Cl₂, regenerating Cl• (propagation): the two steps add up to CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl and repeat thousands of times. Any two radicals meeting end a chain (termination).
alt: A cycle: Cl• reacts with CH₄ to give CH₃• and HCl; CH₃• reacts with Cl₂ to give CH₃Cl and Cl•, which returns to the start. Initiation and termination are shown beside it.
description: Termination: for example Cl• + CH₃• → CH₃Cl, or 2Cl• → Cl₂.
notes: Termination: Cl• + CH₃• → CH₃Cl; 2Cl• → Cl₂; 2CH₃• → C₂H₆
